Listening Practice Guide

This guide covers the four sections of the IELTS Listening paper and the habits that separate a band 6 from a band 8.

Section 1: everyday conversation

Section 1 is a transactional dialogue: booking accommodation, joining a library, arranging a delivery. The answers are almost always names, numbers, dates and addresses, spelled out by the speaker.

Write what you hear, not what you expect. A candidate who assumes the street is "Mill Road" because it usually is will miss "Mill Court".

Spelling traps

Double letters are the commonest loss. Listen for the speaker saying "double e" and for surnames given letter by letter.

Section 4: the academic lecture

Section 4 runs without a break and has no second speaker to slow it down. The note-completion task follows the lecture in order, so if you are lost, find the next heading rather than the next answer.

Signposting language

Lecturers announce structure: "having looked at", "turning now to", "the final point". Those phrases tell you which gap you are on.
